scenes.text: Hello little friend! I'm Clever Mouse Jerry, and today we're going on an amazing journey about transitions. Are you ready to explore changes and how we can adapt to them? Transitions are like little adventures in our everyday lives. Sometimes they can be fun, and sometimes they can be a bit tricky, but I’ll be here to help you understand them better. Let’s get started on this exciting journey together!

Transitions happen when things change, like when you start a new school year or move to a new house. It's like when I find a new cheese tunnel in the wall! At first, it might seem a bit scary because everything is different. But then, I remember that with a little courage and curiosity, I can discover so many new and exciting things. Do you remember a time when you experienced a big change?

Let's think about how we can make transitions easier. One way is to take deep breaths. Let's try it together! Breathe in slowly through your nose, hold it, and then breathe out through your mouth. Taking deep breaths can help us feel calm and ready to face new situations. It’s like when I’m about to sneak past Tom the cat, I take a deep breath and tiptoe quietly.

Great job with the breathing! Now, let’s talk about how being brave can help us with transitions. Being brave doesn’t mean we’re not scared, it means we try even when we feel a little scared. Like when I try to reach the cheese on the top shelf, I feel a bit nervous, but I climb up anyway. You can do it too! Whenever you face something new, remind yourself how brave you are.

Remember when we talked about being brave? Sometimes, having a friend with us can make transitions easier. Friends can be like our cheerleaders, supporting us and making us feel less alone. When I explore a new part of the house, I like to bring my friend, Little Bird, along. Together, we laugh and discover new things, making it a fun adventure. Do you have a friend who helps you with changes?

Let’s think about how routines can help us with transitions. Having a routine means doing things in a set order every day, like brushing your teeth or reading a story before bed. Routines help us know what to expect, which makes new things feel less scary. It’s like when I wake up, I always stretch my whiskers and check my cheese stash. Would you like to create a fun routine together?

Wonderful! Routines give us a sense of stability and help us feel secure. Now, let's talk about how we can celebrate small successes during transitions. Every time you try something new, it’s a little victory! Like when I find a new way to get cheese, I do a happy dance. You can celebrate by clapping your hands or giving yourself a big smile. Every step forward is a reason to be proud!

Now, let’s think about how talking to someone can help us with transitions. Sharing how we feel with a grown-up or a friend can make us feel better. Sometimes, when I’m unsure about a change, I talk to Grandma Mouse. She listens and gives me great advice. Who do you like to talk to when you need some support? Remember, it’s okay to ask for help when things feel a bit tough.

Can you think of a time when you had to adapt to something new? Maybe it was starting a new activity or meeting new friends. How did it make you feel, and what did you do to feel better? Sharing your experiences can help others who might feel the same way. I’m so curious to hear about your adventures and what you learned from them!

Let’s continue by thinking about how being curious can help us with transitions. Curiosity is like a little spark that makes us want to learn more. When I’m curious, I find out all sorts of interesting things, like how to build a new tunnel. Being curious helps us see changes as opportunities to learn and grow. Next time you face a change, try asking questions and see what new things you can discover!

Remember how we talked about asking questions? Asking questions can turn something unknown into something exciting. Like when I didn’t know what was behind the big door, I asked my friends and found out it was a pantry full of snacks! Asking questions helps us feel more prepared and less worried about what’s new. What question would you like to ask about a change you’re facing?

Let’s talk about how practicing new things can make transitions smoother. Practice helps us get better and feel more confident. It’s like when I practice jumping from one shelf to another; each time I get a little better. You can practice by trying small parts of a new activity, like practicing tying your shoes before starting school. Practicing helps us feel ready and excited for what’s to come!

You’re doing great! Now, let’s think about how we can stay positive during transitions. Staying positive means looking for the good things in new situations. Like when I meet a new animal, I think about the fun we might have together. You can stay positive by thinking about all the exciting things you’ll learn and the new friends you’ll make. Remember, every change is a new opportunity to shine!

What’s something new you’re looking forward to? Maybe it’s a new game, a new class, or a new friend. Thinking about the good things helps us feel excited instead of worried. I’d love to hear what you’re excited about and why it makes you happy. Sharing these thoughts can make the transition feel even more exciting and less scary!

Thank you for joining me, Clever Mouse Jerry, on this adventure about transitions! We’ve learned so much about being brave, curious, and positive. Remember, changes are like little adventures that help us grow and learn. Whenever you face a new change, you can use these tips to make it easier and more fun. I’m so proud of you, and I can’t wait to hear about your adventures. Goodbye for now, and see you next time!
